tiles.label: The Sealed Door
tiles.defaultTopic: a room locked from the inside, and no way it could be
tiles.promptSeed: Write about discovering a room locked from the inside with no other way in or out, and the impossible situation found within. Focus on the puzzle of the scene, not the resolution.
tiles.description: A room locked from the inside, and no way it could be.
constraints: End on the impossibility, not the solution

tiles.label: No Way Out
tiles.defaultTopic: trapped somewhere that shouldn't be able to trap anyone
tiles.promptSeed: Write about realizing you're trapped in a space that should have an obvious exit, and the mounting tension of searching for a way out that isn't there.
tiles.description: Trapped somewhere that shouldn't be able to trap anyone.

tiles.label: The Only Witness
tiles.defaultTopic: the one person who saw what happened, and what they're not saying
tiles.promptSeed: Describe the account of the only witness to an event in a sealed space, focusing on what details they emphasize and what they conspicuously avoid mentioning.
tiles.description: The one person who saw what happened, and what they're not saying.
constraints: At least one detail the witness deliberately omits

tiles.label: The Impossible Crime
tiles.defaultTopic: a crime with no apparent way it could have been committed
tiles.promptSeed: Describe, from an outside investigator's perspective, the scene of a crime that appears to have no logical means of having been committed. Present the facts plainly, without resolving the mystery.
tiles.description: A crime with no apparent way it could have been committed.

tiles.label: Years Later
tiles.defaultTopic: reopening a case everyone else has forgotten
tiles.promptSeed: Describe someone reopening a case file that's sat untouched for years, noting what's changed about how the old evidence reads with new eyes.
tiles.description: Reopening a case everyone else has forgotten.

tiles.label: The Unsolved File
tiles.defaultTopic: the details that never added up, laid out one more time
tiles.promptSeed: Describe the contents of an unsolved case file, listing the details that never quite fit together, in a tone of tired, careful re-examination.
tiles.description: The details that never added up, laid out one more time.
constraints: Written as a review of case notes, not narrative scene

tiles.label: New Evidence
tiles.defaultTopic: one new detail that changes everything, or nothing
tiles.promptSeed: Describe the discovery of a single new piece of evidence in a long-cold case, and the immediate uncertainty over whether it changes the whole picture or means nothing at all.
tiles.description: One new detail that changes everything, or nothing.

tiles.label: Buried Truth
tiles.defaultTopic: the thing someone has kept hidden for years, finally surfacing
tiles.promptSeed: Describe a long-buried truth surfacing after years of concealment, focusing on the moment of exposure rather than the original event.
tiles.description: The thing someone has kept hidden for years, finally surfacing.

tiles.label: The Alibi
tiles.defaultTopic: an alibi that's almost too perfect
tiles.promptSeed: Write from the perspective of someone corroborating a friend's alibi, noticing small inconsistencies in the story they're being asked to support, and deciding what to do with that knowledge.
tiles.description: An alibi that's almost too perfect.

tiles.label: Trust No One
tiles.defaultTopic: realizing you can't tell who's telling the truth anymore
tiles.promptSeed: Write about the moment of realizing that everyone around you might be lying about something, and the immediate, disorienting recalibration of who to trust.
tiles.description: Realizing you can't tell who's telling the truth anymore.

tiles.label: The Tell
tiles.defaultTopic: the small, involuntary sign that gives someone away
tiles.promptSeed: Describe watching someone during a conversation and noticing the one small involuntary sign that reveals they're lying, without confronting them about it.
tiles.description: The small, involuntary sign that gives someone away.

tiles.label: Two Stories
tiles.defaultTopic: two accounts of the same night that don't quite match
tiles.promptSeed: Present two brief, conflicting accounts of the same event from two different people, letting the contradictions speak for themselves without resolving which is true.
tiles.description: Two accounts of the same night that don't quite match.
constraints: No narrator judgment on which is true

promptSeed:
[SYSTEM]
You are NarraWeave, a creative writing engine focused on tense, atmospheric mystery and suspense writing in English. Your output withholds and reveals information deliberately, never over-explaining.

[MODE]
Produce only the creative output. No titles, no preambles, no explanations, no meta-commentary. The piece should stand entirely on its own.

[TILE]
{{tile.promptSeed}}

[CONSTRAINTS]
- Output ONLY the creative piece — nothing else.
- Follow the structural rules of the selected form exactly (paragraph and word limits).
- Maintain deliberate ambiguity where the tile calls for it.
- Avoid resolving mysteries the tile doesn't ask to be resolved.
